name: Maryland
standard: WCAG 2.1 AA + Maryland IT Nonvisual Access standards (COMAR 14.33.02)

laws.cite: Md. Code, State Finance & Procurement §3.5-301 et seq. (incl. §3.5-303(c), §3.5-311 Nonvisual Access Clause)
laws.summary: Requires IT procured or provided by executive branch units to be nonvisually accessible and every non-exempt IT solicitation to carry the Nonvisual Access Clause.
Maryland IT Nonvisual Access regulations, effective 2005-03-01, largely based on Section 508 plus Maryland-specific provisions.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: State of Maryland Digital Accessibility Policy (issued 2024-01-08, revised 2025-12-02)

applies_to: All executive branch departments and agencies (and public higher-ed institutions for NVA), internal and external IT solutions developed, provided or procured.

deadlines.what: Maryland policy's stated ADA Title II compliance date (written before the DOJ extension)
ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Verify accessibility before deployment; validation testing by DoIT or MDOD after remediation
Vendor manual + automated testing incl. screen reader and iOS/Android mobile testing
Content vetting so new documents are 'born accessible' (WCAG 2.1 AA)
Staff training within 30 days of hire / 90 days of policy
mobile: explicit — policy requires vendor mobile testing on iOS and Android and DoIT consults on mobile applications.
procurement: Nonvisual Access Clause (SF&P §3.5-311) required in non-exempt IT solicitations; ACRs/VPATs required in solicitations and reviewed by MDOD/DoIT; DoIT sits on the Software Review Board.
enforcement: DoIT Office of Accessibility enforces COMAR 14.33.02; MDOD handles constituent concerns and works with agencies on remediation.
notes: SF&P section text not opened directly; cites are as stated on DoIT pages and in the policy. A search snippet claimed an April 26, 2027 state deadline; not verified in the policy (which says 2026-04-24). Education Article §7-910 (accessible digital materials for students) surfaced in search but was not reviewed.
